declarations.docstring: Precomposing the degreewise biproduct comparison with the first inclusion yields the left resolution map followed by the first inclusion.
The first-inclusion formula for the degreewise comparison remains valid after postcomposition with any morphism.
Precomposing the degreewise biproduct comparison with the second inclusion is the sum of the right resolution map into the second summand and the cross term into the first.
The second-inclusion formula for the degreewise comparison remains valid after postcomposition with any morphism.
Constructs a morphism between the objects associated to short exact complexes with chosen projective resolutions of their first and third terms.
An auxiliary definition whose formal type is unavailable in the displayed signature.
Constructs a morphism from degree zero of the third-term projective resolution to the middle object of the target short complex.
Constructs a morphism from degree zero of the source third-term resolution to the left object of the target short complex.
The degree-zero lift followed by the target's first differential equals the induced morphism to its middle object.
The factorization of the degree-zero middle morphism through the target's first differential persists after postcomposition.
The degree-zero morphism to the target middle object vanishes after composition with the target's second differential.
Constructs a morphism between the complexes assembled from the endpoint projective resolutions of two short exact complexes.
Defines the degreewise morphism between biproducts of the first- and third-term projective resolutions.
Postcomposing the degreewise comparison with the first projection gives the sum of the left resolution component and the cross term on the two source summands.
The formula for the first projection of the degreewise comparison persists after postcomposition.
Postcomposing the degreewise comparison with the second projection gives the right resolution component on the second source summand.
The formula for the second projection of the degreewise comparison persists after postcomposition.
Successive degreewise comparison morphisms commute with the differentials of the assembled complexes.
Defines at each degree a morphism from the source third-term resolution to the target first-term resolution.
The successor cross term followed by the target differential equals the lifting operation applied to the current cross term.
The cross term in the successor degree is the first component extracted from the auxiliary dependent data.
Given a cross term in one degree, constructs a morphism from the next source degree to the current target degree.
At degree zero, the lifted initial cross term vanishes after composition with the target resolution projection.
Constructs the degree-zero morphism from the source third-term resolution to the target first-term resolution.
The initial cross term followed by the target resolution projection equals the degree-zero lift to the target left object.
The projection formula for the initial cross term persists after postcomposition with any morphism.
Constructs the chain map between projective resolutions of the left objects induced by a morphism of short complexes.
Constructs the chain map between projective resolutions of the right objects induced by a morphism of short complexes.
